author: silver state times
title: Nevada baseball team falls to Sacramento State after late comeback attempt
text:
Nevada lost to Sacramento State 13-7 on April 28 in Reno, as the Wolf Pack could not overcome an early six-run deficit at Don Weir Field at Peccole Park.
The game saw Sacramento State (21-25) take control early, scoring three runs in the fourth inning and extending their lead to 9-3 with a solo home run by Jamie Mullin in the fifth. Nevada (23-18) responded in the bottom of the fifth when Mikey Cruz Jr. and Sean Yamaguchi hit back-to-back solo home runs, narrowing the gap to 9-5. Nate Snakenborg followed with a double that scored two more runs, bringing Nevada within two at 9-7.
Snakenborg led Nevada’s offense, finishing with two hits, three RBIs, and a walk. Jayce Dobie also contributed by going three-for-five with a solo home run and extended his hitting streak to 21 games.
Sacramento State regained momentum late in the game by scoring on a wild pitch in the seventh inning and adding three more runs in the eighth. Jakob Poturnak had five RBIs for Sacramento State, including a sacrifice fly and a three-run homer earlier in the game. Erick Dessens added three hits while Mullin finished with two hits and two RBIs.
Mahiro Tomita was charged with the loss for Nevada after allowing five runs over just over two innings pitched. Elijah Rogalski earned his first win for Sacramento State by pitching two innings without giving up an earned run.
Looking ahead, Nevada will return to Mountain West conference play this weekend as they travel to face San Diego State for a three-game series starting Friday evening.
